# Spliffy

> Spliffy is a Node.js web framework on top of µWebSockets.js. Routes are files: a directory of
> `.rt.mjs` handler files and static assets becomes the URL space of the server, like Apache or PHP.
> Package: `@srfnstack/spliffy` (ESM, Node 22 to 26). Version documented here: 1.6.0.

The documentation site (https://srfnstack.github.io/spliffy/) is a client rendered single page app,
so this file is the complete reference, not a table of contents. Everything below is checked
against the 1.6.0 source. The package has no TypeScript types.

## Links

- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/SRFNStack/spliffy): `src/` is small (about 1500 lines) and readable
- [Example app](https://github.com/SRFNStack/spliffy/tree/master/example): every feature below has a route file and a jest test here
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@srfnstack/spliffy)
- [µWebSockets.js](https://github.com/uNetworking/uWebSockets.js): the raw `req`, `res` and `ws` objects come from here
- [Docs site](https://srfnstack.github.io/spliffy/)

## Quick start

```
app/
  serve.mjs
  www/
    index.html          -> GET /            (static)
    hello.rt.mjs        -> /hello           (handler)
    api/
      users/
        index.rt.mjs    -> /api/users
        $id.rt.mjs      -> /api/users/:id
```

```js
// serve.mjs
import spliffy, { moduleDirname } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'

spliffy({
  routeDir: moduleDirname(import.meta.url) + '/www',   // required, absolute path
  port: 10420,                                         // default
  serveRoutesWithSlash: true                           // folder indexes answer /api/users/ as well as /api/users
})
```

```js
// www/api/users/$id.rt.mjs
import { NotFoundError, BadRequestError } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'

export default {
  GET: async ({ url }) => {
    const user = await db.findUser(url.param('id'))
    if (!user) throw new NotFoundError({ error: 'no such user' })
    return user                                        // object -> application/json, 200
  },
  PUT: async ({ url, bodyPromise }) => {
    const body = await bodyPromise                     // parsed by content-type
    if (!body.name) throw new BadRequestError({ error: 'name is required' })
    return db.updateUser(url.param('id'), body)
  },
  DELETE: async ({ url }) => {
    await db.deleteUser(url.param('id'))               // undefined -> 200, empty body
  }
}
```

Run `node serve.mjs`. `spliffy()` returns a promise of the µWebSockets.js app. If any route file
fails to load, the error is logged and the process exits with code 420. Only one `spliffy()` call
per process is honoured, routes are loaded once.

## Route files and URL mapping

Everything is relative to `routeDir`. The scan is recursive and happens once at startup. There is
no hot reload, restart the process after adding files.

| File | URL | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `www/foo.rt.mjs` | `/foo` | the `.rt.mjs` suffix marks a handler module |
| `www/foo/index.rt.mjs` | `/foo` and `/foo/` with `serveRoutesWithSlash` | `index` is the folder itself |
| `www/index.rt.mjs` | `/` | root handler |
| `www/$id.rt.mjs` | `/:id` | a leading `$` makes a path parameter, read with `url.param('id')` |
| `www/users/$userId/posts/$postId.rt.mjs` | `/users/:userId/posts/:postId` | parameters nest through folders |
| `www/files+.rt.mjs` | `/files` and `/files/anything/deeper` | a trailing `+` makes a catch-all |
| `www/logo.png` | `/logo.png` | anything that is not a handler is a static file |
| `www/about.html` | `/about.html` and `/about` | `.html` and `.htm` always resolve without extension |
| `www/docs/index.html` | `/docs`, `/docs/`, `/docs/index`, `/docs/index.html` | index files are the folder default |

Rules and gotchas:

- Accepted handler extensions are `.rt.mjs`, `.rt.js` and `.rt.cjs`. Use `.rt.mjs` (or `.rt.js`
  with `"type": "module"` in package.json). A CommonJS file uses `module.exports = { GET ... }`.
- Only one `$variable` file or folder per directory. Two would be ambiguous and the server refuses to start.
- Files ending in `.test.js` or `.test.mjs` are skipped, so tests can sit next to routes. Set
  `allowTestFileRoutes: true` to change that. `ignoreFilesMatching: ['^draft', '\\.bak$']` skips
  more files by regex on the file name.
- URL matching is done by µWebSockets.js, so a static route wins over a parameter route and a
  parameter route wins over a catch-all.
- Trailing slashes are literal. `foo.rt.mjs` answers `/foo` only, never `/foo/`. A folder index
  (`foo/index.rt.mjs` or `foo/index.html`) answers `/foo`, and also `/foo/` when
  `serveRoutesWithSlash: true` is set. Without it `/foo/` is not found. Every production app sets it.
- A request method with no handler (for example `POST` to a static file, or `HEAD` to a route with
  only `GET`) falls through to the not found handler. Define `HEAD` yourself if clients send it.
  `autoOptions: true` adds an `OPTIONS` handler to every route that answers 204 with an `Allow` header.
- Query strings never take part in routing.

## Handler module shape

```js
export default {
  // reserved, optional
  middleware: [ (req, res, next) => next() ],        // or { ALL: [...], POST: [...] }
  streamRequestBody: false,                          // applies to every method in the file

  // one key per HTTP method, upper case only
  GET: ctx => ({ ok: true }),
  POST: async ctx => { ... },
  PUT: { streamRequestBody: true, handler: async ctx => { ... } },   // per method options
  DELETE: ctx => { ... },
  PATCH: ctx => { ... },
  OPTIONS: ctx => { ... },
  HEAD: ctx => { ... },

  WEBSOCKET: { open (ws) {}, message (ws, msg, isBinary) {}, close (ws) {} }   // see WebSockets
}
```

Allowed keys are `GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE OPTIONS HEAD CONNECT TRACE WEBSOCKET` plus
`middleware` and `streamRequestBody`. Anything else, or a lower case method, fails at startup.
There is no `ALL` handler, `ALL` only exists in middleware objects.

## The handler argument

Each handler receives one context object. Destructure what you need:

```js
GET: ({ url, headers, bodyPromise, req, res }) => { ... }
```

- `url.path`: the request path, no query string, not decoded. For catch-all routes this is the full
  path the client sent, so `url.path.split('/')` is how to read what came after the `+` segment.
- `url.query`: object of query parameters. A key that repeats becomes an array. Values are the raw
  wire bytes unless `decodeQueryParameters: true` is set in the config, which runs
  `decodeURIComponent` on keys and values and turns `+` into a space.
- `url.param(name)`: a path parameter by the `$name` of the file or folder. Never decoded. Call
  `decodeURIComponent` yourself if the value may contain escapes. `url.param` is a closure, so
  `({ url: { param } }) => param('id')` works.
- `headers`: object of lower case request header names to string values.
- `req.cookies`: the parsed `cookie` header as an object, parsed lazily on first access. (A
  `cookies` shortcut exists on the context for routes without middleware only, so prefer
  `req.cookies`.)
- `body`: the parsed request body (see Request bodies), already read by the time the handler runs,
  so a `POST` handler can be synchronous. `null` for `GET` and `HEAD`. With `streamRequestBody` it
  is the `Readable`.
- `bodyPromise`: the same body as a promise, for handlers written around `await bodyPromise`.
- `req`: the spliffy request (see below). `req.user` is the convention middleware uses to attach an
  authenticated principal.
- `res`: the spliffy response (see below). Reading `res` from the context is what switches the
  response into the decorated mode, so a handler that just returns a value never pays for it.

`req` is a `SpliffyRequest`, not a Node `IncomingMessage`:

- `req.path`, `req.url` (path plus query string), `req.method` (upper case), `req.headers`,
  `req.query`, `req.cookies`, `req.get('Header-Name')`
- `req.remoteAddress`, `req.proxiedRemoteAddress` (from the PROXY protocol header, if any)
- `req.spliffyUrl` is the same object as `url` in the context
- The underlying µWebSockets.js request is only valid while the handler is synchronous. Spliffy
  copies headers, path, query and parameters before any `await`, so `req` is safe to use after
  awaiting, but do not keep raw uws request references.
- Set `extendIncomingMessage: true` in the config to put `http.IncomingMessage.prototype` behind
  `req` for middleware such as passport that patches that prototype.

## Returning a response

The return value (or the resolved value of a returned promise) decides the response:

| Returned | Status | Body | Content-Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `undefined`, `null`, `''`, `false` | 200 | empty | none |
| string | 200 | the string | none unless set, so put one in a descriptor |
| `Buffer` | 200 | the bytes | none unless set |
| any other object or array | 200 | `JSON.stringify` | `application/json` |
| `stream.Readable` | 200 | piped | whatever you set |
| descriptor `{ statusCode, statusMessage, headers, body }` | as given | `body` by the rules above | as given |

A descriptor is any object that has at least one of `statusCode`, `statusMessage`, `headers` or
`body`. This is the way to set status and headers from the return value:

```js
GET: () => ({
  statusCode: 201,
  headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html', 'cache-control': 'no-store' },
  body: '<h1>made</h1>'
})
```

Gotchas:

- Because of the descriptor rule, a data object that happens to have a `body`, `headers` or
  `statusCode` key is treated as a descriptor, not serialized as JSON. Wrap it: `{ body: data }`.
- There is no `contentType` key. The content type goes in `headers`.
- Header names are lower cased when stored. `set-cookie` may be an array.
- Alternatively mutate `res` and return nothing or the body: `res.statusCode = 202`,
  `res.setHeader('x-thing', '1')`, `res.setCookie(...)`, then `return data`.
- A `HEAD` route behaves like any other; spliffy does not strip the body for you.

Helpers exported from the package:

```js
import { redirect } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'
export default { GET: redirect('/new-place') }            // 301
export default { GET: redirect('/new-place', false) }     // 302
```

## Errors

Throw to fail a request. Any thrown value ends the response.

```js
import { BadRequestError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, NotFoundError, HttpError } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'

throw new NotFoundError({ error: 'no such thing' })      // 404, body JSON
throw new ForbiddenError('nope')                         // 403, body text
throw new HttpError(418, "I'm a teapot", { short: true })  // any status
```

- Every 4xx and 5xx status has a class named after its reason phrase: `BadRequestError` 400,
  `UnauthorizedError` 401, `PaymentRequiredError` 402, `ForbiddenError` 403, `NotFoundError` 404,
  `MethodNotAllowedError` 405, `NotAcceptableError` 406, `ConflictError` 409, `GoneError` 410,
  `PayloadTooLargeError` 413, `UnsupportedMediaTypeError` 415, `EnhanceYourCalmError` 420,
  `UnprocessableEntityError` 422, `TooManyRequestsError` 429, `InternalServerError` 500,
  `NotImplementedError` 501, `BadGatewayError` 502, `ServiceUnavailableError` 503,
  `GatewayTimeoutError` 504, and the rest. The constructor takes the body only.
- An error with a `statusCode` property is sent with that status. The `body` property is the
  response body; objects are JSON stringified. Any other thrown error is a 500 with an empty body
  and the error is logged with its stack.
- Every error response carries an `x-ref-id` header with a UUID. The same id is passed to
  `errorTransformer` and is meant to be logged so a user facing id can be matched to a stack trace.
- `errorTransformer(err, refId)` in the config runs on every error before it is sent and returns
  the error to send. The pattern used in production apps:

```js
errorTransformer: (err, refId) => {
  if (err.validationErrors) {
    err.statusCode = 400
    err.body = { validationErrors: err.validationErrors }
  } else if (!err.statusCode || err.statusCode === 500) {
    log.error(`500 ${refId}`, err)
    err.statusMessage = `Something went wrong, reference ${refId}`
    err.body = { refId }
  }
  return err
}
```

- Four argument middleware `(err, req, res, next)` runs before the error is sent, see Middleware.

## Request bodies

Bodies are buffered in memory by default and parsed before the handler runs, so `body` on the
context is ready to use and `bodyPromise` resolves to the same value. `GET` and `HEAD` requests
have no body (`null`). For other methods the body is:

| Request `content-type` | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `application/json` | `JSON.parse` of the body (throws, so a 500, on invalid JSON) |
| `text/plain` | string |
| `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` | object, repeated keys become arrays, values decoded |
| `application/octet-stream` | `Buffer`, the bytes as sent |
| anything else, or no header | `Buffer`, unless the bytes look like JSON, then parsed JSON |
| no body | `Buffer` of length 0 whatever the content type (`null` for `GET` and `HEAD`) |

Add or override parsers with `contentHandlers` in the config (keys must be lower case):

```js
contentHandlers: {
  'application/xml': { deserialize: buf => parseXml(buf.toString()), serialize: obj => toXml(obj) },
  'text/csv': { deserialize: buf => buf.toString(), serialize: s => s }
}
```

The same table is used to serialize responses when `res` has a `content-type` the table knows.

`multipart/form-data` is not parsed. Stream it instead:

```js
import Busboy from 'busboy'
export default {
  streamRequestBody: true,
  POST: async ({ headers, bodyPromise }) => {
    const stream = await bodyPromise          // a stream.Readable, nothing buffered
    const bb = Busboy({ headers })
    ...
    stream.pipe(bb)
  }
}
```

With `streamRequestBody: true` (on the module, or on one method with the `{ streamRequestBody,
handler }` form) `bodyPromise` resolves to a `stream.Readable` of the raw bytes. Use this for
uploads of any size; the buffered path concatenates chunks and is meant for small JSON bodies.
There is no built in body size limit, enforce one in middleware or your handler.

## The response object

`res` is the µWebSockets.js response with an Express flavoured layer on top. Use the layer, not
the raw `writeStatus`, `writeHeader` and `cork` calls, unless you know uws.

- `res.statusCode`, `res.statusMessage`
- `res.headers` (object), `res.setHeader(name, value)`, `res.getHeader(name)`,
  `res.removeHeader(name)`, `res.assignHeaders({...})`, `res.writeHead(status, headers)`
- `res.status(code)` (chainable), `res.redirect(location)` or `res.redirect(code, location)`
- `res.send(body)`, `res.json(body)`: finish the response using the return value rules. After
  calling these, return nothing from the handler.
- `res.setCookie(name, value, options)` and the alias `res.cookie(...)`: options go straight to
  `cookie.serialize` (`httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`, `maxAge`, `path`, `domain`, `expires`).
- `res.write(chunk)`, `res.end(body)`, `res.getWritable()`: streaming, see below.
- `res.headersSent`, `res.writableEnded`, `res.ended`, `res.streaming`

Headers are sent with the first `write` or `end`, so set status and headers first.

## Streaming responses

Return a `Readable` as the body, or pipe into `res.getWritable()`:

```js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises'

export default {
  GET: ({ res }) => {
    res.setHeader('content-type', 'image/jpeg')
    return fs.createReadStream('/path/to/pic.jpg')          // simplest
  }
}

export default {
  GET: async ({ res }) => {
    res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/csv')
    await pipeline(rowStream(), res.getWritable())          // backpressure aware
  }
}
```

Writing by hand needs `res.streaming = true` before the handler returns, and you must call
`res.end()` yourself or the connection stays open forever:

```js
GET: async ({ res }) => {
  res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/event-stream')
  res.streaming = true
  const timer = setInterval(() => res.write(`data: ${Date.now()}\n\n`), 1000)
  res.onAborted(() => clearInterval(timer))                 // client went away
}
```

For long lived connections (server sent events, long polling) prefer a WebSocket route; uws
tracks aborted clients for you there.

## Middleware

Express style `(req, res, next)` functions. `req` and `res` are the spliffy objects described
above, not Node's, so middleware that only reads headers, sets headers and cookies, or attaches
properties to `req` works. `helmet`, `passport` and `csurf` are used in production with spliffy.

Three places to attach it:

```js
// 1. config, applies to every route including static files
spliffy({ routeDir, middleware: [helmet(), logRequests] })

// 2. a *.mw.mjs file anywhere under routeDir, applies to that folder and everything below it
// www/api/secure.mw.mjs
export const middleware = { ALL: [requireUser], DELETE: [requireAdmin] }
// (export default { middleware: ... } is also accepted)

// 3. the route module
export default {
  middleware: [requireUser],
  GET: ({ req }) => req.user
}
```

Semantics:

- An array applies to every method. An object maps upper case method names to arrays. `ALL` runs
  for every method, before the method specific list.
- Order: config middleware, then each `.mw.mjs` folder from the top down, then the route's own.
  Several `.mw.mjs` files in one folder run in no guaranteed order, so keep one per folder.
- Call `next()` to continue. Call `next(err)` or throw to fail the request (goes through error
  middleware and `errorTransformer`). Or end the response yourself with `res.end(...)`,
  `res.send(...)` or `res.redirect(...)`, after which the handler does not run. Doing none of
  these hangs the request.
- Async middleware is fine, just make sure every path calls `next()` or ends the response.
- A function with four parameters `(err, req, res, next)` is error middleware. It runs only when
  something threw, after the normal chain and before the error response is written.
- Middleware does not run for `WEBSOCKET` handlers or declarative responses. A route that has
  middleware and exports a declarative response fails to load.
- Static files under a folder with middleware are served through the middleware, which disables
  the declarative fast path for them.
- A route with any middleware takes the slower general path (body is always read before the
  handler runs). Keep hot JSON endpoints middleware free when it matters.

Compression is built in. `compression()` from the package is middleware that compresses responses the
client accepts compressed, brotli first then gzip, for text, json, javascript, xml and svg content
types above a threshold:

```js
import { compression } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'
// www/api/compress.mw.mjs, or in the config middleware for every route
export const middleware = [compression({ threshold: 1024, encodings: ['br', 'gzip'] })]
```

Options: `encodings` [`['br', 'gzip']`] in order of preference, `threshold` [1024] bytes, `brotli`
and `gzip` are passed to zlib (defaults brotli quality 3, gzip level 6), `filter(contentType)`
replaces the content type test. A body sent in one piece is compressed in one call. A body written
in pieces or streamed goes through a zlib stream. Responses that already carry a `content-encoding`
(precompressed static files) are left alone. A `vary: accept-encoding` header is added.

A typical auth middleware:

```js
export const middleware = [
  async (req, res, next) => {
    const user = await userFromCookie(req.cookies.session)
    if (!user) {
      res.statusCode = 401
      res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'unauthorized' }))
      return
    }
    req.user = user
    next()
  }
]
```

## Static files

Any file under `routeDir` that is not a handler or middleware module is served on `GET`:

- Content type comes from the extension. Override or add with `staticContentTypes: { '.wasm':
  'application/wasm' }`.
- Every response carries `ETag` and `Cache-Control`. The default is `max-age=600` (ten
  minutes). Set `staticCacheControl: 'no-cache'` to make browsers revalidate every time, which
  gives a 304 when the ETag still matches. Do this for apps that ship ES modules without hashed
  file names, otherwise a deploy leaves clients running old modules for up to ten minutes.
- Without `cacheStatic` the file is stat'ed and streamed from disk on every request and the ETag
  comes from size and mtime, so edits show up immediately.
- `cacheStatic: true` reads each file into memory on first request and keeps it. The cache follows
  the disk: every request stats the file and a changed mtime, size or inode makes the next
  response read it again, so a replaced file is served on the very next request.
- With `cacheStatic`, files up to `declarativeStaticMaxSize` (64 KiB) are also compiled into
  declarative responses served inside uws with no JavaScript per request. Those cannot compare
  ETags, so conditional requests get a 200 with the full file instead of a 304, and they are read
  once at startup, so a replaced file is only seen after a restart. Set `declarativeStatic: false`
  to keep 304s and follow the disk. Files under middleware, the `notFoundRoute`, the
  `defaultRoute` and files with precompressed twins are never compiled.
- `staticPrecompressed: true` serves a `.br` or `.gz` file sitting next to the original when the
  request accepts that encoding, with the original's content type, a matching `content-encoding`
  and `vary: accept-encoding`. `app.js.br` answers `/app.js` for `accept-encoding: br` and is not a
  route of its own. Brotli is preferred over gzip. The twins are cached and revalidated like the
  original.
- A symlinked directory under `routeDir` is walked like any other directory.
- `index.*` files answer for their folder: `www/app/index.html` serves `/app`, `/app/`,
  `/app/index` and `/app/index.html`.
- `resolveWithoutExtension: ['.js']` makes `/foo.js` also answer at `/foo`. `.html` and `.htm` are
  always in this list.
- `staticMode: true` serves only static files and ignores `.rt.mjs` modules.
- Static routes register `GET` only. Other methods fall through to the not found handler.

## Not found pages and single page apps

Both options name a URL path that must match an existing route (a file in `routeDir`, static or
handler). Spliffy warns at startup when nothing matches.

- `notFoundRoute: '/404.html'`: served with status 404 for any request with no route.
- `defaultRoute: '/index.html'`: served with status 200 for GET requests with no route whose last
  path segment has no file extension. This is the SPA fallback: `/users/42` gets the shell, while
  `/missing.js`, `/img/logo.png` and any POST fall through to `notFoundRoute` (or a bare 404).
- `defaultRouteIgnore: ['/api', /^\/internal\//]`: paths the default route must not answer. String
  entries are prefixes, regular expressions are tested against the path. Those requests also fall
  through to `notFoundRoute`.
- The default route handler sees the originally requested path in `req.path`, so one handler can
  pick between several SPA shells:

```js
// www/default.rt.mjs, with defaultRoute: '/default'
const app = fs.readFileSync(new URL('./index.html', import.meta.url))
const admin = fs.readFileSync(new URL('./admin/index.html', import.meta.url))
export default {
  GET: ({ req }) => ({
    headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html', 'cache-control': 'no-cache' },
    body: req.path.startsWith('/admin') ? admin : app
  })
}
```

- Both must point at a regular handler or static file. A declarative response cannot be the not
  found or default route.
- A folder with an `index.html` can be the target: `defaultRoute: '/ui/'` matches `www/ui/index.html`.

## Serving files from node_modules

`nodeModuleRoutes` exposes individual files from `node_modules` without copying them into
`routeDir`. Files are listed explicitly, there is no glob or pattern support, on purpose.

```js
nodeModuleRoutes: {
  nodeModulesPath: path.join(projectRoot, 'node_modules'),  // optional, see below
  routePrefix: 'vendor',                                     // default: 'lib/ext'
  files: [
    'htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js',                             // -> /vendor/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js
    { modulePath: 'croppr/dist/croppr.min.js', urlPath: 'croppr.js' }   // -> /vendor/croppr.js
  ],
  method: 'copy',                                            // optional: copy into routeDir at startup instead of serving in place
  middleware: [...]                                          // optional, applies to these routes
}
```

- Without `nodeModulesPath`, every `node_modules` directory from `routeDir` up to the filesystem
  root is searched, nearest first, the way node resolves packages. `routeDir: './src/public'`
  finds the project's `node_modules` on its own. Set `nodeModulesPath` only to serve from one
  specific directory; the server then throws `Unable to find node_modules dir` if it is missing.
- A listed file that does not exist is a warning, not an error.
- `method: 'copy'` writes the files under `routeDir/<routePrefix>/...` and they are then served as
  ordinary static files. Add that folder to `.gitignore`.

## WebSockets

Export a `WEBSOCKET` object. It is handed to µWebSockets.js `app.ws()` as is, so every uws
behaviour and option applies. It is registered on every listener, so with `httpsKeyFile` and
`httpsCertFile` the same route answers `wss://` on `httpsPort`.

```js
// www/ws/room/$roomId.rt.mjs  ->  ws://host/ws/room/:roomId
export default {
  WEBSOCKET: {
    idleTimeout: 120,                 // seconds, uws options are allowed here
    maxPayloadLength: 16 * 1024,
    upgrade: (res, req, context) => {
      // req is only valid synchronously here: copy out what you need
      const roomId = req.getParameter(0)                  // path parameters by index
      const key = req.getHeader('sec-websocket-key')
      const protocol = req.getHeader('sec-websocket-protocol')
      const extensions = req.getHeader('sec-websocket-extensions')
      const cookie = req.getHeader('cookie')
      let aborted = false
      res.onAborted(() => { aborted = true })
      authenticate(cookie).then(user => {
        if (aborted) return
        if (!user) return res.cork(() => res.writeStatus('401').end())
        res.cork(() => res.upgrade({ roomId, user }, key, protocol, extensions, context))
      })
    },
    open: ws => {
      const { roomId } = ws.getUserData()
      ws.subscribe(roomId)
    },
    message: (ws, message, isBinary) => {
      const text = Buffer.from(message).toString()         // message is an ArrayBuffer
      ws.publish(ws.getUserData().roomId, text)
    },
    drain: ws => {},                                       // backpressure cleared
    close: (ws, code, message) => {}                       // ws is unusable here, clean up only
  }
}
```

- Omit `upgrade` to accept every connection. `ws.getUserData()` then returns an empty object you
  can write to.
- `ws.send(data, isBinary)` returns 1 on success, 0 when dropped for backpressure, 2 when
  dropped for high backpressure. `ws.getBufferedAmount()` shows what is queued.
- Pub/sub (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `publish`) is process local.
- Middleware does not run for WebSocket routes. Authenticate in `upgrade`.
- `message` and `close` payloads are `ArrayBuffer`s, convert with `Buffer.from(buf).toString()`.
- Spliffy does not add anything to `ws`. See the µWebSockets.js docs for `ping`, `pong`,
  `subscription`, `dropped`, `compression`, `maxBackpressure` and `sendPingsAutomatically`.

## Declarative responses

A handler whose answer is fixed, give or take a value copied from the request, can be described
up front and run entirely inside uws. No JavaScript runs per request, which is faster than any
function handler.

```js
import { declarative } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'

export default {
  GET: declarative()
    .writeHeader('content-type', 'text/plain')
    .writeParameterValue('id')           // path parameter by $name
    .end(''),
  POST: declarative().writeStatus('202 Accepted').end('{"queued":true}'),
  OPTIONS: declarative().writeStatus('204 No Content').writeHeader('allow', 'GET, POST').end('')
}
```

Builder methods: `writeStatus('404 Not Found')`, `writeHeader(name, value)`,
`writeParameterValue(name)`, `writeQueryValue(name)`, `writeHeaderValue(name)`, `writeBody()`
(echo the request body), `write(text)` (a body chunk), `end(text)`. Always finish with `end`, it
returns the compiled response. Status, header names and values are limited to 255 bytes, each
`write` and the `end` text to 64 KiB.

`compileResponse({ statusCode, statusMessage, headers, body })` compiles a fixed response of any
size (a string or Buffer body) into the same form, for example a prebuilt HTML page.

Limits: no middleware on the route, not usable for `WEBSOCKET`, not usable as `notFoundRoute` or
`defaultRoute`, values are copied raw (no decoding).

## Logging

```js
import { log } from '@srfnstack/spliffy'
log.debug('x', obj); log.info(); log.warn(); log.error(err)   // also trace, fatal
```

- `logLevel: 'DEBUG' | 'INFO' | 'WARN' | 'ERROR' | 'NONE'`, default `INFO`. Lines go to the console
  with an ISO timestamp.
- `logger: pino()` (or any object with `trace debug info warn error` methods) replaces the built
  in logger. `logLevel` is ignored then.
- Spliffy writes no access log in 1.5.0. Add config middleware if you need one, and avoid logging
  full URLs when query strings may carry tokens.
- `printRoutes: true` logs every route at startup, useful to check the file to URL mapping.
- Uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections are logged and do not crash the process.

## Full config reference

Only `routeDir` is required. Defaults in brackets.

Server
- `routeDir` absolute path to the route directory, required
- `port` [10420] http port
- `host` [`::`] listen address
- `httpsKeyFile`, `httpsCertFile` PEM files, both or neither. With them a TLS listener (TLS 1.2 and
  1.3, no ALPN) serves every route on `httpsPort`
- `httpsPort` [14420]
- `httpRedirect` [true] with https, `port` answers 301 to the https url. `false` serves every route
  on both ports
- `serveRoutesWithSlash` [false] folder index routes also answer with a trailing slash (`/foo/` as well as `/foo`)
- `autoOptions` [false] generate `OPTIONS` handlers answering 204 with `Allow`
- `writeDateHeader` [false] add a `Date` header, refreshed once a second
- `printRoutes` [false] log the route table at startup
- `middleware` [none] array or `{ METHOD: [...] }` applied to every route

Routing
- `defaultRoute` path of an existing route served with 200 for unmatched extensionless GET requests (SPA fallback)
- `defaultRouteIgnore` [[]] path prefixes or regexes the default route must not answer
- `notFoundRoute` path of an existing route served with 404 for every other unmatched request
- `resolveWithoutExtension` [`['.html', '.htm']`, always included] extensions that also resolve without the extension
- `ignoreFilesMatching` [[]] regex strings tested against file names to skip
- `allowTestFileRoutes` [false] stop skipping `*.test.js` and `*.test.mjs`
- `staticMode` [false] serve static files only, never load handler modules
- `decodeQueryParameters` [false] `decodeURIComponent` query keys and values, `+` becomes space
- `nodeModuleRoutes` [none] see Serving files from node_modules

Static files
- `staticCacheControl` [`max-age=600`] `Cache-Control` for static files
- `staticContentTypes` [{}] `{ '.ext': 'type/subtype' }` additions and overrides
- `cacheStatic` [false] keep file contents in memory, revalidated with a stat per request
- `staticPrecompressed` [false] serve `.br` and `.gz` twins by accept-encoding
- `declarativeStatic` [true] with `cacheStatic`, serve small files from inside uws (no 304s, never re-read)
- `declarativeStaticMaxSize` [65535] largest file compiled into a declarative response

Bodies and errors
- `contentHandlers` [json, text, form, octet-stream] `{ 'type/subtype': { deserialize, serialize } }`.
  `application/octet-stream` bodies are handed over as the `Buffer` that arrived, and an empty body
  is an empty `Buffer` whatever the content type
- `acceptsDefault` [`*/*`] handler used when a request has no `content-type`
- `defaultContentType` [`*/*`] handler used when a response has no `content-type`
- `errorTransformer` [identity] `(err, refId) => err`
- `extendIncomingMessage` [false] give `req` the `http.IncomingMessage` prototype for passport style middleware

Logging
- `logLevel` [`INFO`]
- `logger` [built in]

Not functional in 1.6.0, accepted but ignored: `parseCookie` (cookies are always available),
`decodePathParameters`, `logAccess`, a top level `routePrefix`.

## Package exports

```js
import spliffy, {
  log, redirect, moduleDirname,
  declarative, compileResponse,
  compression, pickEncoding,
  parseQuery, setMultiValueKey,
  HttpError, BadRequestError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, NotFoundError, /* ...every 4xx and 5xx */
} from '@srfnstack/spliffy'
```

- `moduleDirname(import.meta.url)` is `path.dirname(fileURLToPath(url))`, handy for `routeDir`.
- `parseQuery(string, decode)` is the query parser used for `url.query`.
- `compression(options)` is the response compression middleware, see Middleware.
- `pickEncoding(acceptEncoding, ['br', 'gzip'])` picks the first offered encoding the header accepts.

## Project conventions that work well

Seen across several production spliffy apps:

- `routeDir: 'src/public'` for everything the network can reach, `src/private` for database and
  business code imported by the routes. Nothing in `private` is ever served.
- `api/` folder with a `secure.mw.mjs` at its root that authenticates and sets `req.user`, and
  public endpoints (login, health, webhooks) either outside `api/` or allow listed inside the
  middleware by `req.path` prefix.
- A built SPA in `src/public/ui/` with `defaultRoute: '/ui/'` and `staticCacheControl: 'no-cache'`,
  or an `index.rt.mjs` that reads the built `index.html` and sets `cache-control: no-store`.
- Tests next to routes as `*.test.mjs`, started against a real server on a test port.
- `cacheStatic: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` so dev picks up file edits.
- Start script reads `PORT` from the environment and passes `parseInt(process.env.PORT || '10420')`.

## Common mistakes

- Using `query` or `pathParameters` on the context. Use `body`,
  `url.query`, `url.param('name')`.
- Lower case method keys (`get:`) or an `ALL:` handler. Startup fails with a message naming the file.
- Expecting `/foo/` to work. A file route never answers with a trailing slash. A folder index does,
  but only with `serveRoutesWithSlash: true`.
- Returning `{ contentType: 'text/html', body }`. Put the type in `headers`.
- Returning a data object that has a `body` or `headers` key and getting it unwrapped.
- Setting `defaultRoute` and expecting a POST or a request for `/missing.js` to get the shell.
  Only extensionless GETs do; add `/api` style prefixes to `defaultRouteIgnore`.
- Adding a file to `routeDir` while the server runs. The route table is built once at startup,
  so the new file is unknown until a restart.
- Shipping ES modules with `cacheStatic` and the default ten minute `Cache-Control`, then
  deploying. Use `staticCacheControl: 'no-cache'` or hashed file names.
- Forgetting `res.end()` after manual `res.write()` calls, or forgetting `res.streaming = true`.
- Expecting multipart form parsing. Use `streamRequestBody: true` with busboy.
- Keeping a reference to the raw uws `req` inside a WebSocket `upgrade` after an `await`.
- Expecting `decodeURIComponent` on `url.param()` values. Decode them yourself.
